notes: Parity gates (200 iters, G3+G4, same device): seq_graphs bit-identical at G3 (0.0) and 3.3e-11 at G4; seq_compile 2.8e-16 (G3) / 5.3e-12 (G4); eager-rerun CUDA-atomics noise floor 0.0 / 8.1e-15; the functional step-rewrite run eagerly is 0.0 / 4.2e-15. All arms pass the <=1e-9 gate by >1 order of magnitude -- pure reordering, no numerics change; no arm disqualified.

Both section-3.3(ii) capture obstacles resolved as the paper predicted: (a) t%2 alternating-player update -> even/odd CUDAGraph pair (shared memory pool); linear-averaging weight w=t+1 -> 0-dim f64 device tensor advanced in-graph; (b) out-of-place regret/stratsum rebindings -> functional step + copy_ into static pre-allocated buffers (ARM B) / cudagraph-trees-managed pool (ARM A).

ARM A (torch.compile mode=reduce-overhead, fullgraph=True, dynamic=False) compiles the step clean with no graph breaks and no 'skipping cudagraphs' warnings at f64. It required the documented cudagraph-trees feedback-loop contract: torch.compiler.cudagraph_mark_step_begin() before each iteration plus cloning the three state outputs before reuse as inputs (without it: 'accessing tensor output of CUDAGraphs that has been overwritten by a subsequent run' at record time). The 3 clone kernels/iteration stay inside the timed region as honest tooling overhead.

ARM B (manual torch.cuda.CUDAGraph) replays an even/odd graph pair iters times; cross-iteration state is static and mutated strictly in-place; per-iteration intermediates are capture-time allocations from the graph's private pool. It executes the SAME kernel sequence as the eager arm (launch amortization only), which is what makes the G5 graphs-vs-compile split interpretable: graphs isolate launch overhead; compile adds within-tree kernel fusion.

Setup walls excluded from solve timings (symmetric with the section-4.1 precompiled-topology convention) and reported in setup_walls: torch.compile 1.6/5.5/9.3 s per game over all keys, CUDAGraph capture 0.075-0.15 s, topology compile 0.09/0.10/9.4 s (G3/G4/G5).

float64 throughout (mandatory for gated numbers). No f32 row: the eager reference and fused arm live in the gated f64 module (iig_batched.py, untouched), so a like-for-like f32 4-arm table would require dtype-parameterizing the gated kernel -- out of scope for this ablation.

seq_compile beats seq_graphs at G4/G5 (kernel fusion matters once trees deepen); seq_graphs slightly beats seq_compile at G3 (tiny trees: dynamo guard/cache overhead per call exceeds the fusion gain).
New module poker_ai/rebel/iig_batched_graphed.py + runner scripts/run_rebel_cuda_graphs_ablation.py; iig_batched.py and all protected surfaces untouched. Slumbot held out (no interaction).

interpretation.question: How much of the fused-vs-sequential cost-per-solve speedup survives when the per-tree sequential arm gets CUDA-Graphs / torch.compile launch amortization?
interpretation.launch_bound_regime_G4: Amortization lowers the sequential per-tree floor by 72.0% (compile: 202.246 -> 56.587 ms/tree) / 66.0% (graphs), but the amortized arm REMAINS LINEAR in N (slope 56.82 ms/tree) while fused stays flat (m_probe=0.0003); the fused-vs-sequential crossover moves from N*~1 to N*~3.63, and at N=12 fused retains 3.28x (vs 11.6x against eager). The retained advantage still grows with N (~N/3.63): launch amortization rescales the launch-bound speedup by a constant, it does not change its shape.
interpretation.saturated_regime_G5: Pure launch amortization (CUDA Graphs, SAME kernel sequence as eager) recovers only 1.31x of the sequential arm's cost and fused retains 1.85x over it -- consistent with the paper's prediction that capture recovers the launch-gap component but not the short-kernel occupancy component. torch.compile(reduce-overhead), however, ALSO re-codegens/fuses the per-iteration kernels (within-tree kernel fusion on top of graphs), and that stronger tool reaches parity with the eager-ATen fused arm at G5: fused-vs-seq_compile = 1.03x. In the saturated regime the fused arm's residual 2.4x over eager was launch overhead plus eager-ATen kernel inefficiency, not cross-tree co-scheduling; one G5 tree already fills the device.
interpretation.regime_model_restatement: In the paper's min(N, 1/phi) terms: the fused marginal cost m is unchanged by the ablation (G4 m_probe=0.0003, G5 m_probe=0.2488; prior artifact 0.010 / 0.277 -- same regime classifications), while amortization lowers the sequential per-tree floor by 72.0% at G4 and 62.6% at G5 (compile arm; graphs-only: 66.0% / 32.2%). The launch-bound branch keeps its shape with a rescaled slope (speedup ~ N x floor_amortized / fused(1)); the saturated plateau drops from ~2.4x to ~1.0x against the compile arm.
interpretation.claim_revision_for_paper: The honest restatement of the section-4 claims against the strongest launch-amortized sequential arm measured here: G4 (launch-bound) 11.6x -> 3.3x surviving, still scaling with N; G5 (saturated) 2.4x -> 1.03x (parity) against torch.compile, 1.85x surviving against pure CUDA-Graph capture. The eager-dispatch comparisons in section 4 should be labeled as such (they already are), and the section 3.3(ii) prediction is confirmed for pure capture but NOT for compile at G5, where within-tree kernel re-codegen closes the remaining gap.
interpretation.composability_implication_not_a_measurem: At G4 N=1 the amortized single-tree solve (56.587 ms) is ~3.6x faster than the fused arm's own N=1 eager dispatch (201.73 ms): the fused solver is itself eager-dispatched and launch-bound at small scale, so the same amortization tooling can be applied ON TOP of population fusion. The levers compose; the right long-run comparison is amortized-fused vs amortized-sequential, making the surviving speedups reported here conservative lower bounds for the fusion mechanism.
interpretation.update_2026_06_10_amortized_fused_measur: The 'composability_implication_not_a_measurement' paragraph is now a measurement: see the top-level 'amortized_fused' key. Amortized-fused vs amortized-sequential = 7.96x (G3) / 12.06x (G4) / 1.82x (G5); G4 crossover collapses from N*~3.63 back to N*~1.0; the G5 saturated-regime parity verdict (1.03x) reverses to 1.82x under tool symmetry.

G5: the strict gate is UNRESOLVABLE -- the eager fused reference differs from ITSELF by 1.98e-8 between reruns (reproduced 5.7e-9..1.7e-8 over 4 independent reruns; CUDA index_add_ atomics over B=125 cut nodes x 236k infosets amplified through 200 CFR+ iterations). Compile diff 1.98e-8 (1.00x floor), graphs 2.07e-8 (1.05x), and the pure eager step-rewrite WITHOUT any tooling 1.34x floor: all indistinguishable from an eager rerun, no evidence of numerics change beyond reference nondeterminism. interpretation.question: Does the fusion advantage survive when BOTH arms get the best launch-amortization tooling -- amortized-fused vs amortized-sequential (best tool per arm)?

headline.answer: YES -- the launch-bound regime's near-linear fusion advantage fully survives amortized-vs-amortized (G4: speedup ~= N at every sweep point, 11.62x at N=12), and the saturated-regime 'parity' verdict REVERSES (G5: 1.03x -> 1.82x). The prior run's shrunken surviving speedups (2.59/3.28/1.03) were an artifact of the asymmetric comparison (eager-dispatched fused vs amortized sequential); under tool symmetry the fusion mechanism is worth ~N in the launch-bound regime and ~1.8-1.9x marginal at saturation.

interpretation.launch_bound_regime_G4: fused_compile is FLAT across the sweep (55.214 ms at N=1 -> 58.659 ms at N=12, +6.2% for 12x population; slope 0.31 ms/tree on a 55.2 ms floor) while seq_compile remains linear (slope 56.82 ms/tree). Amortized-vs-amortized speedup: 1.02 / 1.97 / 3.97 / 7.84 / 11.62 at N=1/2/4/8/12 -- speedup ~= N exactly, same shape as eager-vs-eager. The amortization levers COMPOSE multiplicatively with fusion (fused_compile is 3.57x over fused_eager at G4, on top of fusion's xN over sequential).
interpretation.saturated_regime_G5: Pure capture is worthless on the fused arm (fused_graphs 1.03x over fused_eager) -- the fused G5 solve is compute-bound, confirming the prior occupancy story. But compile's kernel re-codegen still buys 1.76x (1870.963 -> 1060.313 ms), and the MARGINAL cost per extra tree under compile is 68.04 ms/tree (fused) vs 129.62 ms/tree (sequential): cross-tree co-scheduling retains a ~1.9x marginal advantage even when one tree nominally 'fills' the device. The prior G5 conclusion 'fused-vs-seq_compile = 1.03, one tree already fills the device' compared eager-ATen fused kernels against compiled sequential kernels; under tool parity population fusion is worth 1.82x at N=15, trending to the slope ratio ~1.9x.
interpretation.new_crossover: G4: N* = 1.03 by the prior artifact's formula (best_amortized_fused(Nmax) / best_amortized_seq_slope = 58.659/56.82), interpolated empirical crossing N* = 1.0 -- the prior N*~3.63 collapses back to ~1: amortized fused dominates amortized sequential from N=1 (they coincide there and fused is flat above it). G5: the flat-fused assumption behind that formula is INVALID (amortized fused is not flat, slope 68.04 ms/tree), so its value (8.19) is not a crossover; the measured amortized-vs-amortized speedup is >=1.0 at every N (1.01/1.34/1.60/1.71/1.81) -- NO crossover, dominance from N=1 with the advantage rising toward the marginal-slope ratio ~1.9.
interpretation.m_probe_amortized_fused: G4 fused_compile: m_probe(N=2) = 0.0317, full-span 0.0057 -- still the flat regime (the N2 probe is noisier relative because compile shrank the floor 3.6x; absolute slope 0.31 ms/tree is ~0.5% of the floor per tree). G5 fused_compile: m_probe 0.6885, full-span 0.6211 vs eager 0.2715/0.3849 -- RELATIVE marginal cost rises under amortization because compile cuts the N=1 floor 2.7x (293.7 -> 109.6 ms) but marginal per-tree compute only 1.66x (113.05 -> 68.04 ms/tree). In min(N, 1/phi) terms: amortization raises phi at G5 (the saturated plateau arrives sooner) while leaving the G4 phi~0 launch-bound classification unchanged.
interpretation.regime_model_restated_with_amortized_flo: speedup_amortized(N) ~= (floor_seq + slope_seq*(N-1)) / (floor_fused + slope_fused*(N-1)) with floor_fused ~= floor_seq (same tooling, same granularity at N=1). Launch-bound (G4): slope_fused ~= 0 -> speedup ~= N (measured 11.62 at N=12). Saturated (G5): speedup -> slope_seq/slope_fused = 129.62/68.04 ~= 1.9 (measured 1.81 at N=15). The fusion mechanism's value is the marginal-cost ratio, and it survives -- amortization rescales both arms' floors equally and cannot touch the cross-tree occupancy term.
interpretation.claim_revision_for_paper: The right long-run comparison promised in the prior artifact's composability paragraph is now MEASURED: amortized-fused vs amortized-sequential = 7.96x (G3, N=9), 12.06x (G4, N=12), 1.82x (G5, N=15). The prior surviving-speedup table (2.59/3.28/1.03) understated the fusion mechanism by 3-7x by leaving the fused arm eager-dispatched; section 4 should report the tool-symmetric numbers as primary and the eager-dispatch table as the un-amortized baseline. G5 numbers carry the parity caveat (gate floor-limited at 2e-8 by reference-rerun atomics nondeterminism; arms indistinguishable from an eager rerun).
